text:
Marco Rossi's first full season in Vancouver hasn't found its footing. The ninth pick in 2020, who came over from Minnesota after 202 games as a Wild, has three goals and seven points in 21 games, two points in his last 10, and his ice time has drifted down almost two minutes to about 14 a night. The Canucks have lost a lot of those games, and the five-on-five numbers with him out there are rough: 40% of the expected goals.

Some of that is the team. Evolving-Hockey had him playing with some of the weakest teammates in the league last season and still worth 1.6 wins, 79th among 401 forwards, with most of it on the power play. His own chances this year (0.62 expected goals per 60) match last season almost exactly, and he's shooting 8.3% against a talent range around 13.5%, so a few more should go in. What's missing is the setup work that made him a 2.4-points-per-60 player last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting his own zone with possession 70% of the time, a skill that doesn't show up on a scoresheet.
